title: Microsoft 365 admin center: authoritative SharePoint sites for Copilot Search
summary: The roadmap facts, Microsoft 365 admin center path and PowerShell command are supported. The page overstates visibility as applying to every user despite Copilot Search's user licensing requirement, and its SharePoint UI cell says no control is documented even though the cited release notes describe one.

claims.claim: The Copilot release notes list this feature under 4 November 2026.
claims.quote:
## November 4, 2026
2. **Authoritative content management for Microsoft 365 Copilot Search** [Web]

claims.claim: Authoritative sites identify official, organisation-managed SharePoint sources that Copilot Search recognises as trusted.
claims.quote: Authoritative sites help administrators identify official, organization-managed SharePoint sources. When you mark a site as authoritative, Copilot Search experiences recognize its content as trusted.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Visual signals such as the From your organization label identify trusted items.
claims.quote: Visual signals, such as the From your organization label, make trusted items easier to identify.

claims.claim: The SharePoint feature page says its current-release configuration uses PowerShell and CSOM APIs.
claims.quote: In the current release, configure authoritative sites through PowerShell and CSOM APIs.

claims.claim: The SharePoint authoritative sites article itself provides no admin center designation steps.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint authoritative admin center Mark as authoritative; read sharepoint-authoritative-sites in full. Its configuration sections describe SharePoint Online Management Shell and CSOM, not UI steps.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly stated whether the admin center list and PowerShell designation share their backing list and 100-site limit.
claims.quote: Searched: authoritative Copilot PowerShell admin center list. Read sharepoint-authoritative-sites, copilot-search-admin-experience and release-notes excerpts; none explicitly maps the admin center list to Set-SPOSite or states a shared limit.

claims.claim: The choice of authoritative sites is visible to every user through ranking and the label.
claims.quote: Users without an eligible Microsoft Copilot license receive the Microsoft Search experience when they select the Search module in the Microsoft 365 app.
claims.fix: Replace 'the choice is visible to every user through ranking and the label' with 'users with an eligible Microsoft Copilot licence can see the effect in Copilot Search'. This is the eligibility distinction already documented in Cost and licensing.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The default state of authoritative content management, including behaviour before designation, is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: authoritative Copilot Search default. Read the roadmap, MC1526676, sharepoint-authoritative-sites and relevant release-notes excerpts. None states an initial authoritative list or what this control does before configuration.

claims.claim: Personal sites cannot be marked authoritative.
claims.quote: Personal sites can't be marked as authoritative.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site URL> -IsAuthoritative $true marks the site authoritative using SharePoint Online Management Shell.
claims.quote:
Import-Module -Name Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity "https://<tenant>.sharepoint.com/sites/<siteName>" -IsAuthoritative $true

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: Running Set-SPOSite requires a SharePoint Online administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator and be a site collection administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope
claims.claim: The Set-SPOSite operator must also be a site collection administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator and be a site collection administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.claim: The documented CSOM workflow registers an Entra ID app with Sites.FullControl.All application permissions.
claims.quote: Register-PnPEntraIDAppForInteractiveLogin -ApplicationName "PnP Interactive (SPO Admin)" -Tenant $tenant -SharePointDelegatePermissions "AllSites.FullControl" -SharePointApplicationPermissions "Sites.FullControl.All"

claims.claim: The SharePoint article documents CSOM automation and bulk designation.
claims.quote:
Use CSOM when you need automation or bulk operations.
$results = $tenant.BulkSetResourceAsAuthoritative($siteIds)

claims.claim: The SharePoint authoritative sites article also specifies a 100-site limit.
claims.quote: You can mark up to 100 sites as authoritative.

claims.quote: Changes can take up to 72 hours to appear in supported experiences.

claims.claim: Multi-geo tenants manage authoritative site data per geo.
claims.quote: Multi-geo tenants manage authoritative site data per geo.

claims.claim: Designation is site-level only.
claims.quote: Designation is currently site-level only.

## Prerequisites

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Assigning at least one user a Microsoft Copilot licence provides SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities supporting a Copilot deployment.
claims.quote: If your organization has at least one Microsoft Copilot license assigned to a user, your SharePoint administrators automatically receive access to SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities to support your Copilot deployment.

claims.claim: The linked SharePoint Advanced Management prerequisites include a Microsoft 365 base subscription requirement.
claims.quote:
## Microsoft 365 base subscription
Your organization must have one of the following base licenses:

claims.claim: A user with an eligible Microsoft Copilot licence can access Copilot Search.
claims.quote: If a user has an eligible Microsoft Copilot license, they can access Copilot Search from the Search module in the Microsoft Copilot app.

claims.claim: Users without an eligible Microsoft Copilot licence receive Microsoft Search instead.
claims.quote: Users without an eligible Microsoft Copilot license receive the Microsoft Search experience when they select the Search module in the Microsoft 365 app.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included within the Microsoft Copilot entitlement described in the notes.
claims.quote: If your organization has at least one Microsoft Copilot license assigned to a user, your SharePoint administrators automatically receive access to SharePoint Advanced Management capabilities to support your Copilot deployment.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate authoritative-content meter is published at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: authoritative sites pricing license meter SharePoint Advanced Management. Read sharepoint-authoritative-sites, sharepoint-advanced-management-prerequisites and sharepoint-advanced-management-features-copilot-license; none names a separate authoritative-content meter.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost

claims.quote: Searched: authoritative sites pricing license meter SharePoint Advanced Management. Read the feature article, SAM prerequisites and SAM Copilot feature table; none publishes a price specific to this list. The roadmap names no price.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Microsoft's pages identify no separate add-on specifically for authoritative content.
claims.quote: Searched: authoritative sites pricing license meter SharePoint Advanced Management. Read feature article, SAM prerequisites and SAM Copilot feature table. General SAM add-on options are documented, but no authoritative-content-specific add-on is identified.

claims.claim: No API is explicitly documented as managing the Microsoft 365 admin center authoritative-content list.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Search authoritative Graph API bulk import export; site:learn.microsoft.com/graph authoritative Copilot Search. Read returned search API excerpts, feature article and admin experience page; CSOM is documented, but no explicit admin-list API mapping.

claims.claim: The SharePoint site-designation route has no documented admin UI control.
claims.quote:
Open the SharePoint admin center.
Select a site and choose 'Mark as authoritative site.'
claims.fix: Remove the UI cell's assertion 'Not yet documented'. Replace it with 'The 11 August 2026 release notes describe selecting a site in the SharePoint admin center and choosing Mark as authoritative site; the full navigation path is not documented', linking https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/release-notes#august-11,-2026. Do not invent the missing navigation steps.

claims.claim: The Copilot Search admin experience article covers bookmarks and acronyms but not authoritative content.
claims.quote: Searched: authoritative content within the fully read copilot-search-admin-experience article; no authoritative-site section or setting appears. Its configuration instructions cover acronyms and bookmarks.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises regularly reviewing the list and removing outdated or no-longer-official sites.
claims.quote: Review the list regularly and remove outdated or no-longer-official sites.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes administrator-maintained ranking sources rather than an agent or autonomous action.
claims.quote: Specify and manage SharePoint sites deemed as authoritative content to enhance their relevance and ranking in Microsoft 365 Copilot Search.

claims.quote: When you mark a site as authoritative, Copilot Search experiences recognize its content as trusted.

claims.where: Open questions: bulk import and export

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Search authoritative content import format. Read admin experience article and relevant release-notes excerpts; published CSV fields cover bookmarks and acronyms, not authoritative sites. The authoritative sites article documents CSOM bulk methods, not a file format.
